verdict.rationale: Aider's own docs say it automatically commits every edit with a descriptive commit message and tags the author/committer as "(aider)", which covers staging and commit messages. Creating branches and opening pull requests are not documented as agent capabilities. The /git passthrough only lets the user run raw git commands, which is a user-side workaround and earns no credit. One community comment criticizes the quality of the commit messages but does not contradict that the feature exists. Missing for 10: agent-driven branch creation, pull request opening, explicit staging control, independent corroboration of commit-message quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent stage changes, write commit messages, create branches, and open pull requests

citations.quote: Whenever aider edits a file, it commits those changes with a descriptive commit message.
If aider authored the changes in a commit, they will have “(aider)” appended to the git author and git committer name metadata.
